So when `output_limit IS NULL` — the exact state the design creates for openai.chat_text — `cli` is None and `merged.default.max_tokens` supplies the ceiling. `Config::resolve` loads the GLOBAL ~/.nomi/config.toml at crates/agent/nomi-config/src/config.rs:567 (path built at :832-835) and the project .nomi.toml at :570-575 on the desktop path too — agent.rs:957 calls the same `Config::resolve`, with `project_dir: Some(PathBuf::from(&workspace))` at agent.rs:952. `nomi --init-config` writes `max_tokens = 8192` into that global file today (config.rs:1345-1355, template literal at :1365). `DefaultConfig.max_tokens` becomes `#[serde(default)] Option<u32>`, so a pre-existing `max_tokens = 8192` line parses to Some(8192) and openai.rs:279 inserts it. §10 step 1's assertion "Config::resolve at config.rs:606 finds no [default] max_tokens either" is an unverified environmental assumption presented as a traced step. Compounding it: Phase B item 6 KEEPS the key ("TOML key name unchanged — it is documented user surface"), so after the change `[default] max_tokens` is the only global output-ceiling knob left in the tree AND it overrides a per-model NULL — the knob the owner declared CONFIRMED DEAD survives in the position where it does the most damage.
